items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The Mayor of the Butte Montmartre, M. George Giriel, made me an honorary citizen of the Butte.

ctx.x: Lily and I went to visit some friends in Zurich for three days. A certain Mr and Mrs. Harry Pfister. Harry played sax and was an arranger also. I had met his wife Bettina in Paris when she came there with Felix Debrit for the jazz festival in 1949, and Felix talked to me about leading a band in Chikito. After the visit with the Pfisters, we went to visit Felix in his country home near Bern for three days and came to Paris the 8th of April.

I assisted in one of the post picturesque weddings I had ever seen. This happened in a part of Paris known as the Commune libre de la Butte Montmarte which is the surrounding of the famous Sacred Heart Church (Sacré Coeur). The marriage was that of a well known Gipsy Violinist Roman Jacowlew to a Miss Pilar Gonzales, a spanish actress. After the wedding ceremony, I lead a parade of montmartrois and Montmartroises (as the people from the Butte Montmarte are called) are dressed in picturesque clothes from the last…

A few days later, the Jazz at Philharmonic was giving a concert at Salle Pleyel. I knew weeks before when they would be in town,so Lilly arranged for me to give a cocktail party for them at the reception offices of Ricard, the makers of the well known appetizer. Roy Eldridge, Lester Young, Ray Brown, Joe Benjamin and Norman Grantz the organiser of the J.A.T.P. came to the cocktail. But there is a story about this cocktail that was very embarrassing for me.
